extracted.intended_audience: general readers; researchers seeking company background and controversies
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia article summarizing the history, operations, controversies, and public reception of a private company (MyPillow). Not a how-to or formal guideline document.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unsubstantiated health claims
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of a settlement, MyPillow was banned "from making claims in California that its pillows can cure or treat diseases and their symptoms without a human trial to back up the statements."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not claim products cure or treat medical conditions without human-trial evidence. The page documents prior scientifically unsupported claims (insomnia, sleep apnea, fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis) and a $1M false-advertising settlement enforcing this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose financial connections for endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: The company was banned from promoting itself as the 'official pillow' of the National Sleep Foundation because it failed to disclose its financial connection with the foundation to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claim of an endorsement or 'official' relationship must be accompanied by disclosure of paid or financial relationships; failure to disclose can trigger legal or regulatory action and be treated as deceptive marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional offers must be genuinely time-limited (BBB Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBB's Code of Advertising requires that offers or discounts must be made for a limited time, or the deal becomes the normal price of the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent 'buy one, get one free' or perpetual discounts can violate advertising codes and lead to consumer complaints or enforcement. The article cites class-action and settlement activity related to BOGO promotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not misrepresent professional expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: A class action alleged pillows were falsely advertised and criticized marketing Mike Lindell as a 'Sleep Expert' despite having no board certification or special training in sleep medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid representing individuals as specialists or experts in a field unless they hold appropriate, verifiable qualifications; misrepresentation can form the basis of false-advertising claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales-tax collection and remittance compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The New York State Attorney General charged that MyPillow failed to collect and remit over $500,000 in sales tax; the company later agreed to pay $1.1 million in settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers and advertisers must ensure correct collection/remittance of sales taxes; noncompliance can lead to state enforcement and financial penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making false claims about other companies (defamation risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dominion Voting Systems filed a $1.3 billion lawsuit alleging MyPillow and its CEO made false claims about Dominion's machines, causing irreparable harm to Dominion's reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public statements that falsely accuse or malign other organizations or individuals risk defamation suits and large damages; communications (including press releases) must be fact-checked and legally defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate testimonials and product-benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The company's marketing included testimonials and claims (e.g., easing symptoms of cerebral palsy, acid reflux, menopause) that were challenged in litigation over false advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure customer testimonials and product-benefit statements are truthful, not misleading, and backed by appropriate evidence; misrepresentative testimonials can trigger consumer-law enforcement and class actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with platform rules; avoid ban evasion via corporate accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: MyPillow's company Twitter account was permanently suspended for violating Twitter's policy on ban evasion after the CEO used the company account following his personal ban.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When managing social media and corporate communications, do not use corporate channels to evade platform bans or policies applied to individuals; doing so risks account suspension and reputational harm.
